input: Take a free online typography design course

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Typography is broad — knowing whether they want fundamentals, web typography, print, branding, or advanced type design narrows which course fits best.
Whether this is for personal growth, a professional role, or a client project changes how deep and applied the course needs to be.
Their current skill level (complete beginner vs. some design background) determines the appropriate difficulty of the course.
How many hours per week they can dedicate, and by when they want to finish, shapes which course length is realistic.
Some people learn better through video lectures, others through hands-on projects or reading — the format of the course matters for completion.
Knowing whether they want a certificate, a portfolio piece, or just practical knowledge changes which platform and course structure to prioritise.
Whether they already have a design tool (Figma, Illustrator, Canva, etc.) affects which courses are immediately actionable without extra setup.

gold.taskTitle: Complete a free online typography design course
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to find and complete a free online course focused on typography design.

questions.title: Which area of typography do you want to focus on?
questions.description: Determine whether the user wants fundamentals, web/UI typography, print typography, type for branding, or type design and lettering — so the right course topic is matched.

questions.title: Are you learning this for personal interest or professional work?
questions.description: Understand the purpose — hobbyist curiosity, career development, a specific job role, or a client project — to gauge the required depth and application.

questions.title: How would you describe your current design knowledge level?
questions.description: Establish whether the user is a complete beginner, has some general design experience, or already works in design but is new to typography specifically.

questions.title: How many hours per week can you realistically commit to this?
questions.description: Determine time availability to filter courses by total length and weekly pacing — a 2-hour crash course vs. a 20-hour structured course are very different commitments.

questions.title: Do you prefer video lessons, hands-on projects, or reading-based content?
questions.description: Identify the user's preferred learning format so the recommended course matches how they absorb information best and maximises their chance of completing it.

questions.title: Is earning a certificate at the end important to you?
questions.description: Find out if a shareable certificate of completion matters — for a portfolio, LinkedIn, or a job application — since not all free courses offer one.

questions.title: Which design tools do you already have installed and know?
questions.description: Check whether the user has access to tools like Figma, Adobe Illustrator, Canva, or none — so only courses that match their current toolset are recommended.
